Subject: On-prem air-gapped deployment qualification — recap & next steps

Hi Jane / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap of what we discussed and the action items to keep the on-prem air-gapped qualification moving: 

Summary from today's discovery:
- Primary deployment preference: Private (on-prem) air-gapped environment for production due to regulatory constraints and data residency.
- Short-term: Proof-of-concept using an isolated VPC with Dedicated capacity for eval; long-term: fully air-gapped on-prem install behind the bank network.
- Key constraints: no outbound internet from host, hardware must be on FIPS-compliant firmware, KMS/HSM integration required for key storage, and maintenance windows will be strictly scheduled with offline upgrade capability.

Action items / next steps:
1) Legacy Bank: share HW inventory (exact model, GPU counts, NICs, rackU) and network diagram for the intended cluster — Tom / NetOps to send.
2) Redwood: we'll provide an initial hardware compatibility checklist and a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) covering timeline, milestones, and roles — I'll loop in Dylan for the technical addendum.
3) Schedule deep-dive with NetOps and your security team to validate air-gap/upgrade process and KMS options (HSM on-prem vs Cloud KMS via offline import).

Tentative timeline: aim to have inventory and diagram by EOD Monday (2026-11-22) so our infra team can validate and propose an install profile.

Attachments: none from me yet — Dylan will attach the checklist and sample network diagram in his follow-up.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and commitments from our side:
- We confirm production must be fully air-gapped. No outbound connections from the host are permitted.
- NetOps will share the hardware inventory and the updated network diagram by Monday morning (we'll include GPU model, firmware versions, and rack mapping).
- Regarding keys: our preference is HSM-backed keys (on-prem). We can evaluate temporary cloud KMS only if we can import keys into our HSM during provisioning.
- Maintenance/upgrade windows: typically Saturdays 02:00–06:00 local time; any in-person work needs 2 weeks' notice.

One question for Redwood (copying Dylan): how do you handle offline upgrades for model deltas and runtime patches in air-gapped installs? Do you offer an appliance-style bundle or stepwise upgrade artifacts?

Tom
Director, Platform Ops
Legacy Bank
tom.edwards@legacybank.com | +1 (212) 555-0133

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment qualification — recap & next steps

Tom / Marissa —

Great questions. Short answers and what we'll include in the technical package: 

1) Offline upgrades / model deltas:
- We provide signed, versioned artifact bundles (runtime + model weights) that can be transferred via removable media or secure internal transfer. Each bundle is checksummed and signed with our distro key; you can validate signatures in your air-gapped environment.
- Our recommended approach for frequent model updates is a staged process: test bundle in isolated QA rack -> apply to canary nodes -> roll to production during scheduled window. All steps can be executed offline.

2) Appliance-style options vs stepwise artifacts:
- We support both: (a) a containerized deployable package with orchestration scripts (recommended for teams with existing k8s/on-prem infra) and (b) an appliance-like OVA for customers who prefer a single VM image. We'll include both sample artifacts in the package.

3) HW compatibility / performance:
- Please include GPU model, VRAM, PCIe Gen, and whether NVLink is available; these affect batching and KV cache sizing. Attached is a short HW inventory template (hw_inventory.xlsx) and a network diagram template (network_diagram_v2.pdf) to speed your capture.

4) KMS/HSM integration:
- We support PKCS#11-compatible HSMs and can provide an HSM onboarding guide. For customers that manage keys fully on-prem, we integrate with HSM for sealing model keys and runtime secrets.

5) Support & emergency access:
- For air-gapped installs we offer: a) remote support via Redacted-support playbooks (over a customer-managed jump host), b) on-call for critical incidents (SLA options in MAP), and c) optional on-site support blocks.

I'll attach the checklist and diagrams in this thread. Once you send the inventory, we'll map an install profile and propose required upgrades (if any).

Attachments: hw_inventory.xlsx (stub), network_diagram_v2.pdf (stub)

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
